> **Notional system.** KESTREL is fictional. Its control selection uses NIST's published baselines as a stand-in, as Control Set explains.

# KESTREL Security Controls Traceability Matrix (SCTM)

*Generated by `tools/sctm/build.py` from the CCSD, the SADD, and the curated dispositions in `tools/sctm/dispositions.py`. Edit those, not this page.*

This matrix carries every control in KESTREL's approved set to the SADD outcomes that implement it, the providers it inherits from, and where its evidence is kept. The same rows are kept as OSCAL in KESTREL's system security plan, [`kestrel-ssp.oscal.json`](../06-ssp/kestrel-ssp.oscal.json), under SCTM Automation via Machine-Readable Format (OSCAL) (`GV-5.9.4`).

## Control Set

The CCSD selects KESTREL's controls from the CNSSI 1253 columns for High confidentiality, High integrity, and Moderate availability. This notional example does not reproduce those columns. It uses NIST's OSCAL [High baseline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/usnistgov/oscal-content/main/nist.gov/SP800-53/rev5/json/NIST_SP-800-53_rev5_HIGH-baseline_profile.json) and [privacy baseline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/usnistgov/oscal-content/main/nist.gov/SP800-53/rev5/json/NIST_SP-800-53_rev5_PRIVACY-baseline_profile.json) as a stand-in. The CCSD's tailoring actions then apply. SI-8 is removed with its enhancements, and SR-11(3) and SA-9(5) are added.

That gives 423 controls in the set. The cloud, OT, and IL5 overlays would add rows a real selection carries, and this stand-in omits them.

---

## How to Read Each Row

- **Control ID** and **Control Name** come from NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5.
- **Designation** is System-Specific when KESTREL implements the whole control, Inherited when a provider does, and Hybrid when both do.
- **Implementation Status** comes from the project board, through the SSP's status snapshot. A control is Planned until its outcomes' work starts reaching Done, Partially implemented once some has, and Implemented when every claiming outcome is done. A Hybrid control's status is KESTREL's own part, since the provider's part is already in place.
- **Narrative** says how KESTREL meets the control, naming the products and where they run, in future tense until the work is built. It then gives any provider's part and any CCSD tailoring. Its last sentence links to the part of the [SSP](../06-ssp/index.md) that tells the whole story, and each linked entry closes with its [Security Implementation Plan](../04-sip/index.md) record.
- **Evidence** for every row is kept in the program evidence repository under `evidence/<family>/<control>/`, under Compliance Evidence Collection and Retention (`CO-1.3`). Nothing is collected yet.

## Gaps for the SADD's Gap Register

These rows go to the SADD's gap register (Section 9) for disposition.

**Held but unclaimed (22).** An outcome already does this, or is where it belongs, but its mapping does not claim the control. Each needs a claim added to the outcome, or a recorded reason it stays unclaimed.

| Control | Held By | How |
|---|---|---|
| AC-3(14) | CO-4.2 | The privacy officer handles individual access requests. |
| AU-3(1) | DE-2.1 | Logging adds the detail each source class needs. |
| AU-3(3) | DE-2.4 | Application logs limit the personal information they record. |
| AU-5(2) | DE-3.1 | A silent log source alerts within the hour. |
| CM-3(6) | DA-3.13 | Cryptographic changes go through the KMP and the Configuration Control Board. |
| MA-2(2) | DI-2.4 | Maintenance is scheduled and recorded in Jira Service Management. |
| MA-4(3) | ID-4.7 | Vendor sessions run from the vendor host pool, built to KESTREL's baseline. |
| MA-5(1) | DI-2.4 | Uncleared vendor engineers are escorted at all times. |
| MP-6(3) | DI-5.1 | The media intake station scans media before use. |
| PL-9 | NE-1.1 | Policy as code is defined once and deployed everywhere. |
| PT-5 | CO-4.2 | The account request form carries the Privacy Act statement. |
| PT-5(2) | CO-4.2 | The Privacy Act statement is given where data is collected. |
| PT-7 | CO-4.2 | The PIA identifies any special category of personal information. |
| PT-7(2) | CO-1.1 | Intelligence oversight bars collection on First Amendment activity. |
| SA-8(33) | AI-1.2 | Privacy requirements minimize personal data by design. |
| SA-16 | GV-3.2 | A contract clause requiring developer-provided training belongs in the contract security requirements, still to be confirmed. |
| SA-21 | GV-3.2 | A contract clause requiring screening of developers belongs in the contract security requirements, still to be confirmed. |
| SC-7(24) | DA-1.5 | Data loss prevention watches personal information at the boundary. |
| SI-5(1) | RK-2.3 | CSSP advisories arrive automatically as STIX over TAXII. |
| SI-18 | CO-4.2 | The PIA sets how personal data accuracy is maintained. |
| SI-18(4) | CO-4.2 | The privacy officer handles correction requests. |
| SR-9(1) | GV-3.4 | Supplier assessments cover multiple stages of the supply chain, still to be confirmed. |

**No owner (1).** No outcome or provider holds these.

- AC-18(5)

**Narrow owners (2).** These rest only on narrow outcomes. The SCTM does not read them as system-wide, and each still needs a system-wide owner named.

- CM-6(2): DI-4.1, AI-4.18, AI-9.3 (Partial)
- SA-5: AI-5.8, AI-6.2 (Partial)

### IA: Identification and Authentication

| Control ID | Control Name | Designation | Implementation Status | Narrative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IA-1 | Policy and Procedures | System-Specific | Planned | The program manager will issue the identification and authentication policy as part of KESTREL's system security policy. The Account Management Plan (AMP) will hold the procedures that carry it out, covering authenticators, assurance levels, and sessions. The Configuration Control Board will approve both, and each will be reviewed at least once a year. The SSP describes them under [ID-5.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-51-account-management-plan-amp), [GV-1.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-11-security-policy-framework). |
| IA-2 | Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) | System-Specific | Planned | Every person will be uniquely identified and authenticated before reaching anything in KESTREL. Active Directory in the mission data center will hold each user's account, and Entra ID will authenticate cloud sign-in against a synchronized copy of it. Group or shared accounts will not be used for everyday access. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.3](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-13-centralized-identity-platform). |
| IA-2(1) | Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) \| Multi-factor Authentication to Privileged Accounts | System-Specific | Planned | Privileged accounts will authenticate with a CAC, which combines the card with its PIN. Administrators will sign in with the card first, through Entra certificate-based authentication or Active Directory smart card logon, before CyberArk or Entra Privileged Identity Management grants any privileged role. The directory and station break-glass accounts are the one exception. They use console-only passwords under a compensating control, held by two custodians and changed after every use. CCSD tailoring action 6 (compensating control) applies, pending the AO's approval. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-21-user-authentication-controls). |
| IA-2(2) | Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) \| Multi-factor Authentication to Non-privileged Accounts | System-Specific | Planned | Non-privileged accounts will authenticate with a smart card as well, in every location. DoD users and performers will use their CAC, vendors an ECA credential, and partners a certificate from their own nation's PKI. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-21-user-authentication-controls). |
| IA-2(5) | Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) \| Individual Authentication with Group Authentication | System-Specific | Planned | Built-in administrative accounts on appliances, hypervisors, and the HSMs will be reachable only through CyberArk. An administrator must first authenticate to CyberArk as an individual with a CAC. CyberArk then injects the shared credential into a recorded session, so the administrator never sees it and every use is tied to a person. The SSP describes it under [ID-4.4](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-44-privileged-credential-vaulting-and-session-brokering). |
| IA-2(8) | Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) \| Access to Accounts — Replay Resistant | System-Specific | Planned | Certificate-based authentication will be used for every network sign-in, and it resists replay because each logon proves possession of the card's private key against a fresh challenge. The break-glass passwords are the only authenticators that would not resist replay. They are limited to named local consoles and never cross a network. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-21-user-authentication-controls). |
| IA-2(12) | Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) \| Acceptance of PIV Credentials | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL will accept DoD CACs as PIV credentials. Entra certificate-based authentication will accept them in the cloud, and Active Directory smart card logon on premises. Each card's certificate is validated against DoD PKI and checked for revocation. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-21-user-authentication-controls). |
| IA-3 | Device Identification and Authentication | System-Specific | Planned | Devices will be authenticated before they connect. In the data center and at the alternate site, Cisco ISE will require 802.1X with EAP-TLS on every wired port, using device certificates from the program PKI, and the operating sites will follow in Phase 3. Each aircraft and ground control station will authenticate on the datalinks with its own program PKI device identity. Equipment that cannot hold a certificate will be admitted by its registered hardware address, and only to its own zone. The SSP describes them under [ID-3.7](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-37-otlegacy-device-identity-controls), [NE-1.7](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-17-network-access-control-nac8021x). |
| IA-4 | Identifier Management | System-Specific | Planned | Each person's identifier will be assigned at enrollment and bound to their CAC record, or to their sponsor's record for partners and vendors. IT Operations will assign identifiers through Jira Service Management and Entra ID Governance. Each new account will be checked against existing ones, so no person holds two identities and no identifier is assigned to a second person. The SSP describes them under [ID-1.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-11-identity-proofing-and-enrollment), [ID-1.8](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-18-account-lifecycle-and-identity-data-quality). |
| IA-4(4) | Identifier Management \| Identify User Status | System-Specific | Planned | Each identifier will show the user's status. CAC affiliation will mark contractors, and a nationality attribute will mark partners and other foreign nationals. Roles and access policies can then tell these populations apart. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-11-identity-proofing-and-enrollment). |
| IA-5 | Authenticator Management | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL will manage every authenticator it uses through a defined lifecycle. DoD issues and revokes the CACs, while the program PKI will issue, renew, and revoke device and workload certificates, with its keys in the nShield HSMs and its certificates tracked in Keyfactor Command. Windows LAPS and group Managed Service Accounts will rotate local administrator and service passwords. Vendor-default credentials will be replaced before any server controller or fleet device is fielded. After a confirmed compromise, every affected authenticator will be reset. The SSP describes them under [ID-1.5](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-15-directory-and-tier-0-infrastructure-hardening), [ID-2.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-22-credential-management), [ID-3.7](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-37-otlegacy-device-identity-controls), [DI-3.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-32-secure-compute-baselines), [RS-3.4](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-34-eradication-and-threat-removal). |
| IA-5(1) | Authenticator Management \| Password-based Authentication | System-Specific | Planned | Passwords will remain only on the break-glass accounts. Each password will be split between two custodians, sealed, and changed after every use. The AMP will set its length and composition. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-21-user-authentication-controls). |
| IA-5(2) | Authenticator Management \| Public Key-based Authentication | Hybrid | Planned | Certificate validation will build a path to an approved trust anchor and check revocation at each session. DoD PKI, the External Certificate Authorities, and approved partner PKIs supply the anchors. Services will accept a cached revocation response for up to 24 hours, and the ground control stations will check a local list refreshed daily and before each flight. Private keys stay on the CAC or in the HSMs, and service accounts will authenticate with certificates wherever they can. **Inherited from DoD PKI:** The DoD and External Certificate Authority trust anchors. The SSP describes them under [ID-1.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-12-external-pki-trust-and-sponsorship), [ID-2.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-22-credential-management), [ID-3.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-32-application-and-service-account-identities). |
| IA-5(6) | Authenticator Management \| Protection of Authenticators | System-Specific | Planned | Authenticators will be kept out of code, images, and settings. Each cloud spoke's Key Vault will hold that spoke's secrets, and CyberArk will vault administrative credentials and inject them only into recorded sessions. Pipeline and training jobs will receive short-lived tokens through workload identity rather than stored credentials. The foundation model is reached by workload identity with key-based access disabled, so no API key exists to protect. The SSP describes them under [ID-3.6](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-36-secrets-and-credentials-protection), [ID-4.4](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-44-privileged-credential-vaulting-and-session-brokering), [AP-2.25](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-225-ci-credential-and-secrets-management), [AI-4.19](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-419-training-credential-secrets-management), [AI-8.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-83-third-partyfoundation-model-api-dependency-governance). |
| IA-6 | Authentication Feedback | System-Specific | Planned | Sign-in pages and consoles will hide what a user types and will not say which part of a failed logon was wrong. Failed attempts will be limited as the AMP sets. A ground control station whose aircraft is airborne will delay the next prompt and alert instead of locking the account. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-21-user-authentication-controls). |
| IA-7 | Cryptographic Module Authentication | System-Specific | Planned | Operators of the nShield HSMs will authenticate with smart cards from the HSMs' own card sets, and sensitive key operations will need a quorum of those cards. Software cryptographic modules will authenticate their callers through the identity platform. The SSP describes it under [DA-3.4](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-34-hsm-and-hardware-root-of-trust-management). |
| IA-8 | Identification and Authentication (Non-organizational Users) | System-Specific | Planned | People outside the organization will be identified and authenticated before reaching their part of KESTREL. Vendor support engineers will sign in with ECA Medium Hardware credentials through Entra certificate-based authentication. Partner systems will authenticate to the partner API with mutual TLS, using certificates from their own nation's PKI or an ECA. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-12-external-pki-trust-and-sponsorship). |
| IA-8(1) | Identification and Authentication (Non-organizational Users) \| Acceptance of PIV Credentials from Other Agencies | System-Specific | Planned | PIV credentials issued by other federal agencies will be accepted through the same certificate-based authentication, provided their issuers are on KESTREL's trust list. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-12-external-pki-trust-and-sponsorship). |
| IA-8(2) | Identification and Authentication (Non-organizational Users) \| Acceptance of External Authenticators | System-Specific | Planned | Only external authenticators from issuers on KESTREL's trust list will be accepted. The list names the External Certificate Authorities and each partner nation's issuing authorities, and adding a partner nation requires a CCSD revision. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-12-external-pki-trust-and-sponsorship). |
| IA-8(4) | Identification and Authentication (Non-organizational Users) \| Use of Defined Profiles | System-Specific | Planned | Partner connections will follow defined profiles. Partner systems will use X.509 certificates over mutual TLS. Partner identity providers, when they join in Phase 3, will federate using SAML or OIDC profiles agreed with each partner. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-12-external-pki-trust-and-sponsorship). |
| IA-11 | Re-authentication | System-Specific | Planned | Users will be asked to authenticate again when risk or context changes. Administrative consoles will always require fresh authentication, and activating a privileged role will too. Cloud and VDI sessions will end and require sign-in again when the AMP's session limits are reached, or sooner if continuous access evaluation finds the risk severe. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.6](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-26-continuous-authentication). |
| IA-12 | Identity Proofing | System-Specific | Planned | Every person will be proofed before KESTREL issues an account, at the assurance level the AMP sets for their population. DoD users and performers are proofed through their CAC issuance, and KESTREL binds each account to that record. Partners and vendors will be proofed through a KESTREL sponsor's attestation. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-11-identity-proofing-and-enrollment). |
| IA-12(2) | Identity Proofing \| Identity Evidence | System-Specific | Planned | The evidence behind each enrollment will be recorded in Jira Service Management. For DoD users and performers, that is the CAC record. For partners and vendors, it is the sponsor's attestation and the documents it relies on. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-11-identity-proofing-and-enrollment). |
| IA-12(3) | Identity Proofing \| Identity Evidence Validation and Verification | System-Specific | Planned | IT Operations will validate the evidence at enrollment. Each CAC will be checked against DoD PKI, and each sponsor's attestation against that sponsor's agreement with KESTREL. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-11-identity-proofing-and-enrollment). |
| IA-12(4) | Identity Proofing \| In-person Validation and Verification | Inherited | Inherited | DoD validates each person's identity evidence in person when it issues their CAC. KESTREL relies on that step and does not repeat it. |
| IA-12(5) | Identity Proofing \| Address Confirmation | System-Specific | Planned | For DoD users and performers, CAC issuance confirms the address of record. For partners and vendors, a registration code or notice of proofing will be sent out of band to the address their sponsor records. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-11-identity-proofing-and-enrollment). |
